title: Algorithms Basics
content: An algorithm is a finite sequence of well-defined instructions for solving a class of problems.

title: Data Structures Overview
content: A data structure is a specialized format for organizing, processing, and storing data efficiently.

title: Sorting Algorithms
content: Sorting arranges elements in a defined order using strategies such as divide-and-conquer and merging.

title: Recursion Fundamentals
content: Recursion solves problems by breaking them into smaller self-similar subproblems until a base case is reached.

title: Computational Complexity Theory
content: Complexity theory classifies problems by their inherent difficulty, using big-O notation for asymptotic bounds.

title: Graph Theory Introduction
content: Graph theory studies vertex-edge networks and underpins algorithms for routing, searching, and network analysis.

title: Knuth and Algorithm Analysis
content: Donald Knuth systematized and popularized rigorous algorithm analysis in The Art of Computer Programming, introducing rigorous performance characterization.
